title: Building the Global Environment with Scheme Primitives
description: make_global_env creates an Env pre-loaded with arithmetic, comparison, list, boolean, type predicate, and I/O primitives as Python lambdas. Pairs are 2-tuples, empty list is None.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Arithmetic primitives: + uses sum (variadic), - handles binary and unary, *, /, % are binary. Each lambda takes a list of args.
Comparison primitives: <, >, <=, >=, = all take two args and return Python booleans (which are #t/#f in Scheme).

List operations use 2-tuples for pairs, None for empty list. cons makes a pair. car/cdr extract head/tail. list calls _make_list. null? checks for None. pair? checks for tuple. length, append, map use helper functions.
Boolean: not returns True only if arg is exactly False (Scheme's only falsy value). boolean? checks isinstance bool.
Type predicates: number? (int/float but not bool), symbol? (string not starting with quote), string? (string starting with quote), procedure? (callable).

steps.question: The display primitive at line 45 uses `(print(a[0], end=''), None)[1]`. Why this odd tuple construction instead of just `print(a[0], end='')`?
steps.answer: Scheme primitives must return a value. print returns None in Python, but the tuple `(print(...), None)[1]` evaluates print for its side effect, then returns None explicitly. This makes the return value consistent with other primitives that return None (display returns unspecified in Scheme).

steps.description: newline uses the same pattern: prints a newline, returns None.
_make_list builds a pair-chain from Python args: iterates reversed, wraps each item in (item, result). (1, 2, 3) becomes (1, (2, (3, None))).
Helpers: _length walks the pair chain counting. _append recurses: if first is None returns second, else (head, _append(tail, second)). _map applies proc to each element, building new pair chain.
scheme_list_to_python converts pair chain back to Python list for display: walks the chain collecting heads.
Run it. genv = make_global_env() creates the Env with all primitives loaded.
Tests loop begins. (cons 1 2) calls cons lambda => (1, 2). Prints => (1, 2).
(null? (list)): list with no args calls _make_list([]) => None. null? checks None => True. Prints => True.
(pair? (cons 1 2)): cons => (1, 2) which is tuple => True. Prints => True.
(number? 42): 42 is int not bool => True. Prints => True.
(boolean? #t): #t parses to True, isinstance bool => True. Prints => True.
(procedure? car): car is a lambda (callable) => True. Prints => True.
(list 1 2 3 4) calls _make_list with those arguments => (1, (2, (3, (4, None)))). scheme_list_to_python converts to [1, 2, 3, 4]. Prints as Python list.
